sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Creeping willow is a low, deciduous shrub of European dunes, heaths and other open habitats. Its stems often spread close to the ground and it is usually no more than about 1 m tall.

sections.title: Leaves and catkins
sections.text: The small, oval to oblong leaves vary in hairiness. Like other willows, it bears separate male and female catkins, typically up to about 2–2.5 cm long. The plate shows its creeping branches, narrow leaves and upright catkins.

sections.title: Uses and caution
sections.text: The consulted botanical sources do not establish a food use or a species-specific toxicity profile for this willow.
